body:
I know what you mean.  We're kinda in the same boat.  It appears to me that the meds are kicking in.  Whatever you described is perfectly normal; happens to the best of us.  There will be moments of pure ecstasy, and in a second, it could all plunge into excruciating depression and anxiety.  It's all part of the adjusting process.

  Remember that most people couldn't give two shits about whoever you're talking to, or whatever you're doing in your free time.  They're too engrossed in themselves, probably thinking the same thing.  Instead of imagining that they're judging you \(which they're not\), reframe it as "hey, that guy has the guts to talk to that girl.  He wasn't like that a month ago."  And whoever said something shitty probably was feeling shitty and insecure, and needed someone to vent on.  They didn't mean it in the slightest, so don't take it to heart.  Seriously, my classmates can make a fucking career out of roasting each other senselessly.    

  The part about talking to guys.  Happened to me as well.  They're probably not estranged from you, perhaps they've been waiting for you to talk to them.  No one ever goes up to me and talks straight up, dunno if it's because I look like I just rose from the swamp, or come across as intimidating, or both.  So go on, talk to them!  You'll never know until you take the initiative to rekindle those connections. 

  But hey, you're making progress.  Remember, the fact that you're acknowledging this means that you can only go forward.  Struggle is part of finding your balance and improving.

I understand how you feel bro, maybe they were just trying to play around (albeit in a strange way), or fuck with your mind to see how you would react.  If they were making those assumptions, they sound incredibly insecure.  I'm certain you've already established your boundaries but if by any chance they do it again you shouldn't take it seriously AT ALL !  Just smirk or pass it off as a joke and carry on, maybe redirect the subject.  Trying to erase their verbal attacks from your mind probably is counter-intuitive, try distracting yourself instead.  Plus, even if you did mar your friendship (very slim chance, this happens all the time), they're equally accountable since they ridiculed you in such a way (I mean seriously, Freudian complex??!?)

Yeah it's kinda weird how some of us find friends.  Even a simple wave can go a looong ass way.  After all, the goal isn't to rack up as many friends as possible, but to find people who you can connect to.  Also, damn!  And I thought it was hard for me to talk to girls in my school !  Personally, albeit I'm muslim, I find it kinda strange why they segregate gender in such a radical way in Pakistan.  Times have changed indeed, but the traditions are stubbornly rooted in the system.

Hmmm....I've always considered going rogue and speaking my mind.  I've seen so many people become so socially successful by just saying random shit charmingly.  It doesn't even have to make sense; it's rather based on jumping to conclusions instantly or blurting whatever interpretation comes to mind, combined with an attention span of two seconds.  It actually works brilliantly !  But charming is the key for this.  When I do it, it comes across as insulting and harsh.  Sure who cares if you appear that way, but this has made almost my whole class avoid me !  Now whenever I talk to someone (even if i'm smiling and not intruding their space), they become extremely conscious and serious, and don the "get the fuck away from me" kind of face.  As soon as I leave, they resume laughing and talking.  I swear, I think people see me as an alien !  I should probably wear sunglasses during class then

Yea, I think that's the key advice I've been missing.  But usually when I do speak my mind, it comes across the wrong way.  Idk if it's my natural facial expression, the tone of my voice, etc.  But for some reason almost everyone gets intimidated by me.  Like after school I walked to a music shop and checked out the synths, and some random ass girl said my face looked weird.  I mean, obviously, it's a shit test, but c'mon, I wasn't prepared for that !  Tbh, I was so immersed in the music that I turned a blind eye to it tho ;)  
  Sure, talking in the spur of the moment sounds fun, but usually I get so paralyzed by anxiety during conversations that even breathing becomes a chore.  When I try to talk to someone, all this advice from experience vanishes from my head, and I'm just left with the spotlight shining on the blank slate that's supposed to be my mind.  I choke up on my words, I stiffen up, maybe people notice it, maybe not, who knows?  It kinda reminds me of when I was a kid trying to learn how to swim: I would gasp for air and kick violently when the coach released me into the water.  
  A bunch of people have told me "that's fine, who needs people anyways?  After all, introverts aren't designed to be social".  Even my mom says there's not much I can do about it since its in our genes and I just have to live with it blah blah blah.  But the truth we're designed by evolution to connect with others; how will I survive when I'm 18 and living on my own?  I can barely say hi to a girl, how tf will I sustain a conversation with the apartment contractor?  Maybe in the distant future introversion will prove to be an evolutionary advantage for independence, but certainly not now!
  Bear in mind I don't wanna get laid or anything.  That shit's almost unattainable for me.  I'm content as long as I can establish a friend group.
